analysis.summary: Brazil sit on one point after a 1-1 draw with Morocco in their opener and face a Haiti side that lost 0-1 to Scotland. For Brazil, three points against the group's weakest opponent is effectively non-negotiable to stay on course for the knockout stages. The quality gap is enormous: Brazil's depleted but still world-class attack featuring Vinicius Jr, Raphinha, and Endrick faces a Haiti side that created chances against Scotland but failed to convert, and will be significantly outmatched by a Brazil side highly motivated to restore confidence.
analysis.home_form: Brazil drew 1-1 with Morocco in their World Cup opener (Vinicius Jr equaliser). In the five pre-tournament matches: lost 0-1 at Bolivia (Sep 2025), won 5-0 vs South Korea (Oct 2025), lost 2-3 vs Japan (Oct 2025), won 2-0 vs Senegal (Nov 2025), drew 1-1 vs Tunisia (Nov 2025). Mixed form but strong attacking depth. Key absences: Neymar (calf, likely entire group stage), Rodrygo (ACL, tournament out), Estevao (hamstring, tournament out), Eder Militao (hamstring surgery, tournament out). Ancelotti fields a 4-2-3-1 / 4-2-4 setup with abundant forward options.
analysis.away_form: Haiti qualified for the World Cup for the first time since 1974, winning Concacaf Group C. Last five competitive matches: drew 3-3 at Costa Rica (Sep 2025), won 3-0 vs Nicaragua (Oct 2025), lost 0-3 at Honduras (Oct 2025), won 1-0 vs Costa Rica (Nov 2025), won 2-0 vs Nicaragua (Nov 2025). At the World Cup, lost 0-1 to Scotland despite showing attacking intent (51% possession, 13 shots). Warm-ups: won 4-0 vs New Zealand, lost 1-2 vs Peru. Key players: Duckens Nazon (striker), Danley Jean Jacques (midfield), captain Johny Placide (goalkeeper). Coach Sebastien Migne favours a 4-3-2-1.
analysis.h2h: Brazil lead the all-time head-to-head 3 wins from 3 meetings, scoring 17 goals and conceding just 1. Most notable: Copa America 2016, Brazil 7-1 Haiti (Coutinho hat-trick). Earlier meetings: Brazil 6-0 Haiti (friendly, Aug 2004) and Brazil 4-0 Haiti (friendly, Apr 1974). Haiti have never defeated Brazil and have never even drawn with them.

key_factors: Brazil are under strong tournament pressure after drawing with Morocco — a loss or draw here would put last-16 qualification in serious doubt, maximising motivation
Historical dominance is extreme: Brazil have beaten Haiti 4-0, 6-0, and 7-1 in all three previous meetings
Vinicius Jr is Brazil's primary attacking threat and consistently exploits space behind defensive lines — Haiti's right-hand side is likely the target
Haiti showed courage vs Scotland (more possession, 13 shots) but failed to score and face a dramatically superior opponent in Brazil
Brazil's attack remains potent despite absences: Vinicius Jr, Raphinha, Endrick, Matheus Cunha, and Gabriel Martinelli all available
Philadelphia venue: neutral in feel, moderate altitude, no significant heat or travel disadvantage for either side
Ancelotti expected to rotate some starters (e.g. Casemiro may sit) but the attacking unit should be close to full strength
Haiti's 4-3-2-1 deep-block strategy could initially frustrate Brazil, but their defensive quality against elite attacking movement is unproven at this level
